summary: AuthConfig is used to configure authentication for vendor APIs that require a token before other API calls can be made. It involves setting up client IDs to manage token generation.
steps: Identify the client that requires AuthConfig.
Change the ID of that client to set up AuthConfig.
business_rules: Some APIs are open, while others require a login/token for access.
AuthConfig is typically used when a login API is called to obtain a token, which is then used for subsequent API calls.
important_notes: Currently, only one client in the system utilizes AuthConfig.
questions: What is AuthConfig and when is it used?
How do I set up an API that requires authentication using AuthConfig?
